analysis.one_liner: Jindal Steel Limited (formerly Jindal Steel & Power) makes steel in Chhattisgarh and Odisha, selling plates, rails, structural steel and other long/flat products, and is mid-way through a large capacity expansion at its Angul plant.
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on 23 October 2026 (four days from now) to approve Q2 FY27 results. In the quarter just reported (Q1 FY27, June 2026), consolidated profit fell roughly 44% year-on-year to about ₹844 crore, mainly because a planned blast-furnace refractory shutdown cut production by around 300,000 tonnes and because finance costs and depreciation rose sharply as newly built capacity (a 1,050 MW power plant, new furnaces) got capitalised onto the books. Standalone PAT for the same quarter was reported separately at about ₹1,086 crore - the two numbers use different consolidation bases and should not be confused with each other.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a steel maker that is spending very large sums (tens of thousands of crores) to roughly double capacity at one plant, funded partly by debt and partly by profits. The tension: this quarter's profit dropped sharply even though the company is growing production, because the new assets add depreciation and interest costs before they add proportionate revenue. Whether that bet pays off depends on debt levels coming down as planned and the new capacity actually running at full output. The stock trades at a much richer multiple of earnings than it used to, which raises the bar for what the expansion needs to deliver.
analysis.quarters: FY26 full year: record production of 9.25 million tonnes (+14% YoY), PAT of about ₹3,361 crore. Q4 FY26 (Mar 2026) swung from a loss of ₹304 crore a year earlier to a profit of roughly ₹1,041-1,045 crore - a large base-effect turnaround, not a smooth trend, so the prior year's loss should be read as the anomaly rather than this quarter as a breakout. Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) consolidated PAT fell to about ₹844 crore versus ₹1,496 crore a year earlier (-44%), with EBITDA down about 11.5% YoY to ₹2,660 crore (margin ~17.2%). Management flagged a one-off refractory shutdown (~300,000 tonnes of lost output) and higher finance/depreciation charges from newly capitalised assets as the drivers - both are genuine, named reasons rather than vague excuses, but they mean this quarter's profit decline is not purely an operating problem. Revenue figures differ across sources (gross vs net revenue basis) by a few thousand crore; treat any single revenue number with that caveat.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down about 19% from its 21 April 2026 peak of ₹1,286.5 to the current ₹1,041.8, but it remains above its 52-week low of ₹984.24 - this is a drawdown within a normal trading range, not evidence of a corporate-action distortion (the company's last stock splits were in 2003, 2008 and 2009, all long settled and already reflected in the price history). Over 1 year the stock is up only 3.79%, trailing both the Nifty's -11.43% comparison point loosely and badly trailing peer JSWSTEEL's +9.01%. Over 3 years it has returned 58.2%, behind the peer's 63.97% but well ahead of the Nifty's 17.12%. Over 5 years it has returned 140.69%, well ahead of both the peer (88.86%) and the Nifty (24.27%). Over 3 months it has actually outperformed both (+1.0% vs peer -1.25% and Nifty -5.57%). The pattern is a strong long-run holding but a recent period of underperformance versus its closest peer.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of about 34.6x and P/B of about 2.09x, the stock trades well above its own history - EV/EBITDA is 13.96x versus a 3-year average of 9.46x. Why it looks expensive: the market appears to be pricing in the payoff from the ongoing capacity expansion (crude steel capacity rising to 15.6 million tonnes once Angul's new blast furnace and BOF-3 ramp up), not current earnings, which just fell YoY. Whether that premium is justified is a separate question from the fact of it - it depends on the new capacity delivering volume and margin that current ROE (8.22%) and ROCE (9.70%) don't yet show.
analysis.growth_read: Growth has been genuinely volume-led so far - FY26 production hit a record 9.25 million tonnes (+14% YoY) and sales volumes rose 9% - alongside a modest margin/mix improvement as value-added products rose to 66% of the sales mix (from 61% in Q4 FY26). The company is in the middle of a large, multi-year capex program (₹37,457 crore spent of a planned ₹47,043 crore) aimed at nearly doubling Angul's capacity to 12 million tonnes. Management has guided FY27 capex of ₹8,500-10,000 crore and says future spending will target downstream, value-added capacity rather than more raw commodity steel capacity - a reasonable sign of capital discipline, but one to watch given overall returns on capital remain under 10%.
analysis.health_read: Net debt stood at about ₹15,927 crore as of Q1 FY27 (one data aggregator shows a lower ₹13,757 crore for March 2026, likely from different netting of lease liabilities - company-reported figures are the more reliable basis), giving a net debt/EBITDA of 1.71x, with management targeting below 1.5x by Q2 FY27. Debt-to-equity is a moderate 0.45x, and credit raters (CARE, ICRA) both upgraded the company to AA+ in mid-2026, suggesting lenders see improving credit quality even as debt funds the expansion. ROE of 8.22% and ROCE of 9.70% are thin for a company carrying this much capex and debt - the central risk here is business risk (whether the new capacity earns an adequate return once fully ramped) more than acute financial/liquidity risk, since the balance sheet and credit ratings currently look manageable. Not verified - check on Screener for operating cash flow conversion versus reported PAT.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold about 62.71% (flat quarter-on-quarter as of June 2026), with roughly 9.92% of that promoter stake under pledge - a meaningful, non-trivial figure, though trending down slightly after one promoter entity (Beaufield Holdings) released part of its pledge in mid-2026. FII holding has declined over the past year, from 9.43% (Sept 2025) to 8.84% (June 2026), while domestic institutional holding has risen from roughly flat levels to 19.52%, suggesting domestic funds have been net buyers as foreign investors trimmed. No marquee or celebrity individual investor was found on the shareholding register in available sources - if you were expecting to see one, it is not confirmed as present. September 2026 shareholding data has not yet been published.
strengths: Record FY26 production of 9.25 million tonnes, up 14% YoY, with sales volume up 9% to 8.68 million tonnes
Credit rating upgraded to AA+ by both CARE (Jul 2026) and ICRA (Aug 2026), reflecting improving perceived credit quality
Net debt/EBITDA has fallen from 4.56x in FY20 to 1.71x now, even after ₹42,409 crore of cumulative expansion spending since FY20
Value-added product mix rose to 66% of sales in the latest quarter from 61% the prior quarter, indicating some margin-mix improvement alongside volume growth
watchpoints: Consolidated Q1 FY27 PAT fell about 44% YoY to ₹844 crore on a one-off refractory shutdown and rising finance/depreciation costs - watch whether Q2 FY27 (due 23 Oct 2026) shows these costs persisting as new capacity scales up
ROE of 8.22% and ROCE of 9.70% are low for a company undertaking a ₹47,043 crore capex program - returns need to improve materially to justify the current 34.6x P/E
About 9.92% of promoter shareholding remains pledged - not resolved, only partially reduced in 2026
EV/EBITDA of 13.96x is well above the 3-year average of 9.46x, meaning the stock already prices in a successful capacity ramp-up that has not yet shown up in reported returns
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due 23 October 2026, specifically whether net debt/EBITDA falls to the targeted sub-1.5x and whether EBITDA/tonne recovers from the Q1 one-off shutdown - this will show whether the capex cycle is starting to convert into the earnings the current valuation already assumes.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked production, capex, debt and credit-rating facts across Business Standard, screener.in, company filings and rating agency announcements, which were broadly consistent. Revenue figures diverge across sources by a few thousand crore (likely gross vs net revenue presentation) and net debt has a roughly ₹2,000 crore gap between company-reported and one aggregator figure - company-reported figures were used as primary. One source (ScanX) reporting Q1 FY27 PAT 'up 35% YoY' contradicts multiple other sources showing a ~44% decline and was treated as an outlier and excluded. Jindal Power Limited (JPL) was divested in 2021 and is not a subsidiary - any reference to a 'JPL steel plant' is a misconception; the expansion is on Jindal Steel Limited's own books at Angul. Operating cash flow conversion was not independently verified - check on Screener.
